purpose: Candidate retrieval and exact source-scoped features.

object.definition: There are $M$ clients interacting simultaneously in $\mathbb R^d$ for $T=L_{\mathrm{comm}}R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds each. They synchronize once every $L_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds, for $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ synchronizations. Each $f_t^m:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and convex, with uniform Euclidean Lipschitz constant $G$ on the whole space. $$f_t(x)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x),\qquad \frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\|\nabla f_t^m(x)-\nabla f_t(x)\|_2^2\le\zeta^2\quad(\forall t,x).$$ The adversary may depend on all past actions and the algorithm, but not on its current private randomness. All clients share the same hindsight comparator: $$x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\|x\|_2\le B}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x).$$

feedback_quality.coupling: simultaneous pair; second query cannot adapt to first value
feedback_quality.feedback: two exact values of the same current local function per client/round
feedback_quality.noise: no measurement noise; random directions induce estimator variance

operation.query_signature: Each client simultaneously submits $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ and receives exact values of the same current local function at both points. The second point cannot depend on the first response. There is no independent measurement noise; variance from randomized directions is part of the estimator analysis. Both query points incur loss. The comparator ball $\{x:\|x\|_2\le B\}$ does not restrict all queries. Inputs $M,d,T,L_{\mathrm{comm}},R_{\mathrm{comm}},G,B,\zeta$ are public. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

response_signature.coupling: simultaneous pair; second query cannot adapt to first value
response_signature.feedback: two exact values of the same current local function per client/round

definition.clients: M clients in R^d; T=L_comm R_comm rounds per client
definition.losses: f_t^m:R^d->R convex differentiable and G-Lipschitz globally
definition.comparator: one common x_star in Euclidean ball radius B minimizing sum_{m,t} f_t^m(x)
definition.heterogeneity: (1/M) sum_m ||gradient f_t^m(x)-gradient f_t(x)||_2^2<=zeta^2 for every x,t
definition.environment: adaptive to all prior played points and algorithm, not current private randomization

steps: Each client submits $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ simultaneously in every round, then receives exact values of the same current local function at those two points.
The second point cannot depend on the first response. There is no independent measurement noise; variance from randomized directions is part of estimator analysis.
Both query points incur loss. The comparator ball $\{x:\|x\|_2\le B\}$ does not constrain all query points.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
protocols.adversary_information: adaptive to all prior played points and algorithm, not current private randomization
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Each client outputs two simultaneous query points $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ per round, and both incur local loss. The comparator constraint $\|x\|_2\le B$ does not constrain these query points. Loss cannot be recomputed afterward at their center or average.
protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
